precepts.text: And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people. We go to our people just like the forefathers did, and we bring the Bible with us. We do not just go to one city or one state; wherever our people are scattered and afflicted, we are there.
precepts.point: Video played from a 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, filmed in Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family could live: residents said they would be afraid to go out at night, that you really could not trust any of them, and one said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march I don't like. They do not like when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Tatum claimed he had not seen black Hebrew Israelites going out and saying anything in the community when a black man died. That is a lie; he has been found a liar. That is what we do literally every week. We teach in the hoods and the ghettos where our people are: O Block in Chicago, East St. Louis, Memphis, Miami, Compton, LA, Philly. We go toe to toe and face our people.

“And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.”

They taught in Judah: we go to our people just like the forefathers did. They had the book of the law of the Lord with them: we bring the Bible with us. They went throughout all the cities: we do not just go to one city or one state. Wherever our people are scattered, wherever our people are being afflicted, we are there, teaching the people.

precepts.text: Asa slept with his fathers and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.
precepts.point: He strengthened himself against Israel, setting himself apart from the northern kingdom's ways.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.”

Kings tells the same succession: Jehoshaphat reigned in the place of his father Asa, taking the throne after him. And Chronicles adds what he did first: he “strengthened himself against Israel”, setting himself apart from the northern kingdom's ways.

precepts.text: Teach them the ordinances and laws and show them the way wherein they must walk.
precepts.point: The way we must walk is defined by the ordinances and laws we are taught.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.”

The way we must walk is defined by the ordinances and laws we are taught. Jehoshaphat walked that way: he “sought to the Lord God of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Israel.”

precepts.text: Go out into the highways and hedges and compel them to come in.
precepts.point: They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.”

That is what Jehoshaphat's princes and Levites did. They “had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.” It is the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

precepts.text: Doth not wisdom cry and understanding put forth her voice.
precepts.point: They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?”

Wisdom cries out to the people. That is what the teachers Jehoshaphat sent out did: they carried the book of the law of the Lord through all the cities of Judah “and taught the people”, putting forth the voice of understanding where the people were.

precepts.text: She standeth in the high places, at the gates, at the entry of the city.
precepts.point: They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“She standeth in the top of high places, by the way in the places of the paths. She crieth at the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors.”

Wisdom does not stay hidden; she goes where the people are, to the gates and the entry of the city. So did the princes and Levites who “went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people”, and so do we, going out into the streets to teach.

precepts.text: Wisdom's call is unto men and her voice to the sons of men, a rally cry for men.
precepts.point: They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.”

Wisdom's call is unto men, a rally cry for men. Jehoshaphat sent men, his princes, Levites and priests, to teach in the cities of Judah with the book of the law of the Lord.

precepts.text: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men in the city.
precepts.point: Teaching the Law had a real effect on the nations; wisdom disarmed his enemies.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty men which are in the city.”

Teaching the law had a real effect on the nations. After the book of the law went through the cities of Judah, “the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.” Wisdom strengthened Judah more than mighty men could.

precepts.text: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroyeth much good.
precepts.point: Teaching the Law had a real effect on the nations; wisdom disarmed his enemies.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.”

Wisdom disarmed Jehoshaphat's enemies. He did not win by weapons of war; the fear of the Lord fell on the kingdoms round about, “so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.”

precepts.text: A poor wise man by his wisdom delivered a little city besieged by a great king.
precepts.point: Teaching the Law had a real effect on the nations; wisdom disarmed his enemies.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city.”

Wisdom delivers where strength cannot. Judah taught the law in all its cities, and the fear of the Lord fell upon the kingdoms round about, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat. Wisdom disarmed his enemies.

moments.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord. Remember when we read about Uzziah, it said his heart was lifted up to his destruction. Jehoshaphat is not described that way. It says his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord. This is good pride. Jehoshaphat wanted to accomplish all the things the Lord told him. He wanted to rebuild the city, he wanted to get rid of the idols. This is the type of pride that we want to have.
Moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Judah.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: The updated twelve tribes chart was shown: Judah among the American blacks, with kindred communities from the Igbo of Nigeria to Liberians, Malagasy, Sierra Leone, the Kikuyu of Kenya, the Abayudaya of Uganda, the Falasha of Ethiopia, indigenous groups of North Africa, the Songhai and Ashanti of Ghana, and the Wasambaa of Tanzania. The history is vast, and the chart does not even include the northern kingdom tribes.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

points: So what Christ did in sending out the twelve was not new, and what IUIC is doing is not new. In Jehoshaphat's day our people were worshiping Moloch, Chemosh, and Baal, and the remedy was to tear down the groves and send teachers through the land with the book.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

points: King Jehoshaphat took away the high places and groves out of Judah, the false idols and their little churches, and in the third year of his reign he sent his princes, with Levites and priests, to teach in the cities of Judah. And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.

The Lost Tribes a Myth, by Allen H. Godbey (1930): hundreds of thousands of slaves were brought to America from western Africa, and the author asks how much more of Judaism survived among West African Negroes in that earlier time; as persecuted communities they were more in danger than other groups of being raided by war parties and sold as slaves, and it may be considered certain that many partially Judaized Negroes were among the slaves brought to America. On the Cabinda coast was a group of black Jews known as Mavumba, connected by Ratzel with a colony of Jews expelled from Portugal to Sao Tome, where in 1484 King John II offered the Jews of his dominion the alternative of baptism or exile to the island. The book also records Bishop Matthew's claim of an immemorial Jewish ancestry that is Negro, and a Sierra Leone preacher's sermon from about 1860 teaching that Adam and Eve were colored people.

History read on Liberia: between 1822 and the late 19th century roughly 15,000 to 16,000 free black Americans and formerly enslaved people were relocated to Liberia by the American Colonization Society, a group of white politicians, philanthropists, and slaveholders, some of whom hoped removal of free blacks would strengthen slavery. The settlers arrived with a superiority mentality, set up a Masonic lodge as the gate to political office, and the country later suffered two civil wars totaling fourteen years. Never listen to anyone who says there are no Israelites in Africa; they are there in abundance. Do a little research; read a book.

Jews in Africa: in Mali, several thousand people in Timbuktu claim Jewish ancestry from Moors and Jews fleeing persecution in Spain who migrated south in the 14th century; Askia Muhammad came to power in 1492 and forced Jews to convert to Islam or leave, after which Judaism became illegal in Mali. In Nigeria the Igbo may descend from ancient Semitic and later Jewish migrations, with groups tracing to Gad, Zebulun, and Manasseh; in western Ghana the House of Israel community traces descent through Ivory Coast; in Uganda the Abayudaya practice Judaism; in Somalia the Yibir, the Hebrew tribe, are looked down on as descendants of Israelites; a tribe in Rusape, Zimbabwe claims ancient Jewish connections; and some 40,000 members of the Lemba tribe still claim Jewish roots. Old Jewish communities south of the Atlas Mountains are named in synagogue archives in Cairo, and Jewish, Arab, and Christian accounts cite Jewish rulers of tribal groups scattered throughout Mauritania, Senegal, the western Sudan, Nigeria, and Ghana.
